mcqs.question: Consider two identical steel spheres released simultaneously in two different fluids at the same temperature: (i) water (viscosity η₁) and (ii) motor oil (viscosity η₂), where η₂ > η₁. Which statement correctly compares their terminal velocities?

options.A: The sphere in water reaches a higher terminal velocity than in oil.
options.B: The sphere in oil reaches a higher terminal velocity than in water.
options.C: Both spheres attain the same terminal velocity because they have the same size and density.
options.D: Neither sphere reaches a terminal velocity; they keep accelerating indefinitely.

mcqs.answer: The sphere in water reaches a higher terminal velocity than in oil.
mcqs.explanation: Terminal velocity vₜ = (2r²(ρ_s-ρ_f)g)/(9η). A larger viscosity η gives a smaller vₜ. Since motor oil is more viscous than water, the sphere falls slower in oil, so the water case has the higher terminal velocity.

mcqs.question: Which of the following does NOT significantly affect the viscosity of a liquid at a given temperature?

options.C: External pressure applied to the liquid.

mcqs.answer: External pressure applied to the liquid.
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity of liquids is mainly governed by temperature, intermolecular forces, and molecular geometry. Pressure has a negligible effect compared with these factors, especially for liquids under normal conditions.

mcqs.question: Viscosity of a fluid is best defined as:

options.A: The ratio of shear stress to the rate of shear strain in the fluid.
options.B: The density of the fluid per unit volume.
options.C: The ability of a fluid to conduct electricity.
options.D: The speed at which a fluid flows under gravity.

mcqs.answer: The ratio of shear stress to the rate of shear strain in the fluid.
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity (η) quantifies internal friction: η = τ / (du/dy), where τ is shear stress and du/dy is the velocity gradient (rate of shear strain). This definition captures the resistance to relative motion between fluid layers.

mcqs.question: The coefficient of viscosity (η) of a fluid has the dimension of:
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity is measured in Pascal·second (Pa·s). Since 1 Pa = 1 N·m⁻² = kg·m⁻¹·s⁻², multiplying by second gives kg·m⁻¹·s⁻¹. The other options correspond to different physical quantities.

mcqs.question: Viscous force acting on a moving plate differs from the drag force on a solid object in that:

options.A: Viscous force is proportional to the area of contact and velocity gradient, whereas drag force depends on the shape and Reynolds number.
options.B: Viscous force acts only in gases, while drag force acts only in liquids.
options.C: Viscous force is independent of the fluid’s viscosity, whereas drag force increases with viscosity.
options.D: Both forces are identical in magnitude and origin.

mcqs.answer: Viscous force is proportional to the area of contact and velocity gradient, whereas drag force depends on the shape and Reynolds number.
mcqs.explanation: Viscous force (F = η A (du/dy)) arises from shear between layers and scales with contact area and velocity gradient. Drag force on an object involves pressure drag and skin friction, depends on shape, size, and flow regime (Reynolds number). The other statements are incorrect.

mcqs.question: A small steel ball is dropped into a tall column of glycerin. After a short time it moves at a constant speed. Which statement correctly describes this constant speed?

options.A: It is the terminal velocity, where the weight of the ball is balanced by the upward viscous drag and buoyant force.
options.B: It is the maximum speed the ball can ever attain in any fluid.
options.C: It occurs because the ball has stopped accelerating due to reaching the bottom of the column.
options.D: It is the speed at which the ball’s kinetic energy equals its potential energy.

mcqs.answer: It is the terminal velocity, where the weight of the ball is balanced by the upward viscous drag and buoyant force.
mcqs.explanation: When a falling object reaches terminal velocity, the net force becomes zero: weight = buoyant force + viscous drag. The constant speed observed in glycerin is therefore the terminal velocity. Options B, C, and D describe unrelated or incorrect concepts.

mcqs.question: Which of the following pairs correctly identifies the fluid with higher viscosity at 25 °C?

options.A: Honey and water – honey has higher viscosity.
options.B: Alcohol and glycerin – alcohol has higher viscosity.
options.C: Mercury and oil – mercury has higher viscosity.
options.D: Air and carbon dioxide – air has higher viscosity.

mcqs.answer: Honey and water – honey has higher viscosity.
mcqs.explanation: At room temperature, honey is much more viscous than water. Alcohol is less viscous than glycerin, mercury is less viscous than typical oils, and gases (air, CO₂) have much lower viscosities than liquids, making the other options incorrect.

mcqs.question: During an oil spill on the sea surface, the oil spreads slowly compared to water. This behavior is primarily due to:

options.A: The high viscosity of oil relative to water.
options.B: The lower density of oil compared to water.
options.C: The surface tension of water being greater than that of oil.
options.D: The chemical reactivity of oil with seawater.

mcqs.answer: The high viscosity of oil relative to water.
mcqs.explanation: Viscosity measures internal friction; oil’s higher viscosity resists flow, causing it to spread more slowly than water. While density and surface tension also influence spreading, the dominant factor for the rate of spread is viscosity. Chemical reactivity is not relevant here.
